newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUGUST 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUGUST 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
TRAIN PASSENGERS ESCAPE BOMB BLASTS

Passengers of a Delhi-bound train escaped a powerful bomb explosion that missed the train by seconds about 120 km from Guwahati in Assam state. The explosion on the railway track was suspected to have been triggered by Bodo extremists. The engine driver said he suddenly saw the explosion about 10 meters ahead of the engine, pressed the emergency brake and stopped the train. Five coaches of the train derailed. One of the passengers received minor injuries. The Rajdhani Express was running much slower than its normal speed at 60 km an hour as there was a speed restriction near Sarupetia railway station, the engine driver said. Authorities in Guwahati on Sunday had warned that the Bodo militants would strike in a big way before Independence Day.
The Economic Times
BOURSE INDICATOR ZOOMS BY 83 POINTS

The Bombay bourse's Sensitive Index jumped to an intra-day high of 4,482.51 before closing at 4,481.30, up 83.76 points. The market shrugged off a three-day negative run as investors entered into fresh commitments by buying shares with no delivery period. Investors stepped in to purchase group B1 and B2 shares. Brokers said the activity picked up around the time the National bourse closed for the day.
PERMISSION TO RAISE $1.5 BLN VIA EXTERNAL BORROWINGS

The Finance Ministry cleared $1.5 billion of external commercial borrowings of more than 10 years maturity proposed by six leading companies -- TELCO, Essar Steel, Larsen and Toubro, Ispat, Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation and Steel Authority of India. The permission was given under a recently liberalised regime recommended by a committee. The committee had said external commercial borrowings of over 10 years should be freed completely and taken out of the overall external commercial borrowing quota. Finance Ministry officials said the government was encouraging more long-term commercial debt as it lent greater stability to the country's external sector.
MINISTRY PONDERS DUTY ON MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICES OF SHOES

The Excise Department recommended that the Finance Ministry levy excise duty based on the maximum retail price on high priced shoes. The department has collected data showing that top multinational shoe makers like Reebok, Adidas and Nike are selling most of their shoes at a maximum retail price (MRP) with an average mark-up of 133 percent, 115 percent and 129 percent respectively over the ex-factory price. The MRP provision was introduced to target cases where the difference between the value on which excise is paid and the MRP is very high. The MRP is the maximum price at which a pair of shoes is sold to the consumer. It includes advertising and marketing costs as well as margins and profits.
Financial Express
EUROPEAN COMMISSION REOPENS INVESTIGATIONS

The European Commission reopened an investigation into the exports of unbleached cotton fabrics from India to European countries. The government plans to take the matter to the dispute settlement body of the World Trade Organisation. The Commission has selected major Indian textile companies like the Mafatlals, Century Textiles, Coats Viyella, Vardhman Spinning and Virudhunagar Mills as samples for the probe. Sources in the Textile Ministry said the sample companies were asked to furnish details of domestic and export sales within 40 days.
BOURSE REGULATOR TO REVIEW MODIFIED CARRY FORWARD TRADING

The board of the Securities and Exchange Board of India meets in Bombay on Tuesday to take up a range of issues affecting the capital market. They include a review of regulations over mutual funds and merchant bankers, a review of primary and secondary market regulations and the Varma Committee's recommendations on the modified carry forward system. It will also take up issues like separating fee- and fund-based activities of merchant bankers, increasing the net worth of category I merchant bankers from 50 million rupees to 150 million rupees or doing away with the categories altogether.
SINGAPORE FIRM ORDERS PROBE INTO ASIAN PAINTS DEAL

Capital International of Singapore is believed to have asked one of its brokerage houses operating in India to probe the purchase of a large chunk of Asian Paints shares. The shares were bought by the company along with Morgan Stanley Asset Management. Morgan Stanley later walked out of the deal when it realised that Atul Choksey, from whom they bought the shares, was opting out of the company. The deal was brokered by DSP Merrill Lynch Securities on August 1. Merrill Lynch was trying to settle the deal amicably. Neither Morgan Stanley nor Capital International has formally announced the deal is off.
Business Standard
FOREIGN INSTITUTIONAL INVESTORS ALLOWED FORWARD COVER

The Reserve Bank allowed Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) to buy forward cover for investments in debt instruments. The extent of the cover will be limited to the current market value of the investments in debt instruments translated in dollar terms. The maturity of the cover will not exceed the remaining period to maturity. The premia rates are expected to rise once the FIIs start covering their investments in debt instruments. But since the Reserve Bank has not made any forward cover provision for investment in equities, the premia rates are not expected to move up substantially.
The Observer
RESTRICTIONS ON FABRIC IMPORTS TO BE EASED

India will put 83 trade lines related to fabrics on the Open General Licence from January 1, 1998, as part of her package to remove quantitative restrictions on imports. This will include cotton fabrics, coloured yarn fabrics, synthetic fabrics and woollen fabrics. Textile Ministry sources said both the Textile Ministry and the Commerce Ministry had approved the proposal. The United States and the European Union were pressing India to allow the import of textile products without linking them to any kind of import licence.
NORMS FOR USED TYRE IMPORTS ANNOUNCED

The government announced a ceiling of minimum value for import of used tyres despite the Industry Ministry's recommendation that there should be a ban on the import of second-hand tyres. A notification by the Director General of Foreign Trade said a ceiling of $175 per tyre CIF will be imposed on the import of used tyres for buses, trucks, heavy vehicles and light commercial vehicles. A minimum CIF value of $25 and above per tyre will be imposed on import of tyres of cars, jeeps, three wheelers and two wheelers. The tyre dealers wanted the restriction on tyre imports to be removed. But tyre manufacturers wanted a total ban on imports of used tyres.
Business Line
AMERICAN DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS FLOTATION PROPOSAL REJECTED

The Finance Ministry rejected a proposal by a few major Indian corporates to launch Level-I and Level-II American Depository Receipts (ADRs) as it involved the free dual flow of capital. The government is yet to accept the two-way fungibility, implying free inflow and outflow of capital. Finance Ministry officials said there were problems on account of two-way fungibility and until capital account convertibility was in place it was difficult to clear the proposals. The ministry cleared a couple of proposals from corporates to launch ADRs where there is only one-way flow of capital, officials said.
